value: 'the workflow is the stages, but dependencies can be outside influences. so we can't represent dependencies directly by just saying workflow. each workflow step should list it's dependenices. so BUILD might be gated on BUS DEVICE and EMBEDDINGS GENERATOR... and just be listed like: [ ] BUILD - Needs: - BUS DEVICE - EMBEDDINGS GENERATOR etc. then whenever we look at the state of the things, if there's an update we mark it: [ ] BUILD - Needs: [DONE] BUS DEVICE - EMBEDDINGS GENERATOR — even if we don't pick up the ticket! the fact that we went and looked gets compiled into the ticket.'

value.a: PER-STAGE, NOT PER-TICKET — and this is what makes it storable at all. CC argued against a stored `waits_on` on the grounds that ordering is GOAL-RELATIVE (the same ticket sits differently depending on whether we aim at the librarian or elsewhere), so a stored edge freezes one target's answer. That objection is real and it does NOT apply here: 'BUILD needs the bus device' is intrinsic to that stage, true regardless of the goal. The goal-relative part — the ORDER — is still derived at ask time; only the intrinsic need is stored.

THE MARK IS AN OBSERVATION, NOT A CHECKBOX. {status, when, how measured} — the same three fields a VALIDATION carries, and the same reason a host-seam carries a re-runnable verify and a seal that expires. This shape surfaced TWICE in one session from unrelated directions (here, and as the staleness marker a cached embedding needs), which is evidence it is a primitive in this system rather than a local convenience.

IT RIDES THE STATE/HISTORY SPLIT THAT ALREADY EXISTS. An observation is append-only truth (history); the current mark is a compiled view (state). So this needs no new storage mechanism — it needs the projector's append door, which as of 2026-07-25 also has a shape gate to refuse a malformed mark. The per-component schema declaration filed on that door is exactly the edge this node pulls.

DIVERGENCE FROM THIS TICKET'S OWN FILED DISTINCTION, ARGUED NOT ASSUMED. The cast said marks ride the projector's append door. They do not, and cannot yet: that door writes a COMPONENT's history.json/state.json pair and a staged ticket has neither — a ticket's voyage freezes into history when it PROVES OUT (CLAUDE.md), so routing marks there would mint a history file per staged ticket and invert that design. The mark lands in the ticket record through one function (needs.mark), reusing the projector's discipline (validate-before-write, append-only, atomic write) rather than its file pair. AND IT DELIVERS THE WHY BETTER: because the mark rides INSIDE the ticket, it MIGRATES when the ticket berths beside its code — which is precisely the 'dependency record destroyed by finishing the work' failure this node exists to fix.

`MISSING` IS CC'S COINAGE AND IS FLAGGED FOR RATIFY. Akien's sketch has [DONE] and unmarked; it has no word for 'we went and looked and the thing is NOT there'. That case is the whole point of 'even if we don't pick up the ticket', so it needs a status. DONE is his word, kept. MISSING is mine — derivable in the native domain (a dependency that is not there is missing), but mine until he rules. Owed a ratify-or-reject, like `crossing`.

BUILDING THE CONSUMER IS WHAT TESTED THE CLAIM. needs.py binds to a node's stage vocabulary, which meant parsing 17 live workflow strings for the first time — and only 6 could be parsed at all, with a 7th parsing to FICTION (see the trouble). The chokepoint's own proof said 'the state vocabulary is physics, not /sorted's prose'; it was prose on 11 of 17 nodes. The generalisation worth keeping: a claim that something is physics is only tested when a SECOND reader depends on it, because the first reader can be wrong in the same direction as the writer.
